I04. Secret Passage.name: I04. Secret Passage
I04. Secret Passage.text:
The iridescent walls of this passage appear to be natural in origin - delicate traceries of colored light that merge into each other. The elves here have enhanced the effect by delicately carving the threads of light into fantastical abstract designs that ebb and flow with the passage walls.

The passage to Yldaris has been illumated with the same iridescent lighting as was found in the Farm with Extras level.

The same iridescance is opposite the hidden rock door to the secret tunnel, as a vague hint regarding where to find the door on the opposite wall.

I also added the same otherworldly music that also appears in I20 Meditation Cave, to increase the ambiance.

I03 Yldaris Trading Post.name: I03 Yldaris Trading Post
I03 Yldaris Trading Post.text:
Yldaris is described as a town, but it lacks even one trader.

Therefore, I transformed one of the stalls in I03 Stable into a general-purpose trader.

This shop is generally restocked with merchandise from the Darklands, so they would be interested in any items not usually found in the Darklands, such as those made from genuine surface wood, materials like pearls, cotton and wool, herbs and spices, leathers, horns and poisons derived from surface creatures — the possibilities are limitless.

Likewise, the store should be stocked with more Unusual and Rare items than the usual general store, as long as they could have conceivably originated in the Darklands. Also, it has items through level 12.

After Falxi returns and recovers, he starts to serve as the proprietor. Therefore, his token is in this area.

Introduction.name: Introduction
Introduction.text:
There are only a few changes to this level.

  • I added the @UUID[.0z0cU9Ar4bQHOTzS]{I03 Yldaris Trading Post} to the stable area.

  • I added more of the iridescent lighting to the @UUID[.0lB9gy2KE3dywLcM]{I04. Secret Passage}.

  • I tweaked the lighting in the @UUID[.Ww64ifw5Ss4FI0rT]{I20 Meditation Cave}.

  • I made some encounter changes to @UUID[.yPMmE1qa5s1fflhO]{I31. The Barrens}, and added some cavern walls to narrow the exit passage.

A Note on the Remaster Changes

The Pathfinder game system is replacing the original inhabitants of the Darklands with Ayindilar, or cavern elves. I am assuming those changes will eventually perculate to Abomination Vaults. In the meantime, I have begun to refer to them as cavern elves, and have attempted to make this change througout these journals. Actors will retain the original names until replaced in Abomination Vaults.

I20 Meditation Cave.name: I20 Meditation Cave
I20 Meditation Cave.text: I tweaked the lighting here to make the ghostly light move much more slowly and to replace the crystal lighting effect to Starlight. I just thought a more subtle effect would be more medatative.

I31. The Barrens.name: I31. The Barrens
I31. The Barrens.text:
Changes here support some changes in Lv. 09 Hunting Grounds. I added lighting effects and additional cavern walls to make the passage narrow.

The reason for the passage changes is in I51 Ravirex's Fen, where I replaced the original black dragon with a neutral horned dragon. Ideally, the heroes will heed the elves's warning and stay close to the northern wall until they have spoken to the horned dragon.

Daemonic Fog

I added lighting effects to the fog, and I added an etherial door to the passage beyond, because visibility is supposed to end at 30 feet.

Until the Derghodaemon is defeated, the fog will persist.

Use this macro to clear the fog and visibility to the passage beyond.

@UUID[Macro.RrBgsxcAd7CAnmjY]{Clear Daemonic Fog}

Shadow Malice's Last Show.name: Shadow Malice's Last Show
Shadow Malice's Last Show.text:
In my own playthrough, the Shadow Malace band members hung out on the 4th level until the way to Yldaris was clear.

Then, my heroes arranged for them to pass through to the Darklands.

I added a couple of inactive lights and sconces to the back of the Yldaris Trading Post (aka I03 Stable) so they can have one last show.

Before the leave, one of the members, Gulzash, will offer to trade his Battle Lute to one of the heroes in exchange for a decently runed blade.

Lv. 9 Side Quest - A Deal-Making Dragon.name: Lv. 9 Side Quest - A Deal-Making Dragon

First Impression.name: First Impression
First Impression.text:
The dragon will come out when the heroes first explore the area outside his lair, or after they have defeated all the daemons that are besieging the hunting lodge.

In my own game, I had the dragon make his appearance by taking a nap on the roof of the hunting lodge until the heroes showed up.

Wherever he encounters them, he will lift his head from a nap, study the heroes, and say:

Greetings.

He will pause to see how the heroes react, and if they return his greeting.

I realize that my very presance tends to alarm humanoids such as yourselves, but I trust, giving all you have accomplished, you will not be too alarmed at a parley with a dragon, hmm?

If they ask him how he came to be here, he will offer this brief story:

I have only been here a short while. I heard that there were many challenges here, including a dragon. Since I have been in search of a hunting ground for myself, I came to look over the area. The dragon immediately challenged me, and although it gave a good fight, it could not withstand my horn, among other things. I shoved its carcass into the lake for the abberations there to devour, and I took over its paltry hoard.

It is an unacceptable lair since I do not spend my time wallowing in mud. I am looking for another that is more suitable.

At some point, the players will probably wonder what the dragon wants.

There is something you can do for me. Several somethings, in fact. And I have something you need, a certain unique lens, which is very valuable to Belcorra. If it is valuable to her, then it must be valuable to you as well.

I propose a series of trades — your services in excahnge the lens, and certain other choice items from my hoard, which you will find useful.

You will not find the things I ask for to be dishonorable, and perhaps they are tasks that you would have to undertake anyway. But I would prefer that you undertake these tasks my way, and therefore, it is worth the payment I will offer.

He will then wait to see if they wish to listen to his offer. If they do, proceed to @UUID[.26VLQ8gEu18pv2Mk]{The Dragon's Deals}.

The Dragon's Deals.name: The Dragon's Deals
The Dragon's Deals.text:
The dragon has several trades in mind.

  • To prove he is making an honest offer, he will offer information on the two other humanoid structures in the area:

    • "There is a structure built into the cavern, with a narrow ledge and doorway overlooking the lake. I never never see anything come or go from it."

    • "There is a bridge leading from a narrow passage to an island where a wallowing aberration had corrupted what appeared to be once a garden. Surely there is some kind of structure beyond the narrow passage that is of interest to your kind."

  • In exchange for the Ochre Fulcrum Lens, the dragon asks the heroes to eliminate the demon in the Barrens.

    • "If it teleports away, you will be able to pursue it down the narrow tunnel, whereas I am not. Just proceed down the tunnel until it narrows to a twisting passage, and then kill it behind that point."

  • In exchange for a flight over the lake to and from the structure with the narrow ledge, he wishes to cull the numbers of the deadly fish in the lake, and at the same time, to observe how they fight on land. He will lure the creatures to the shoreline, where the heroes will fight them.

    • "I think any boating expedition would be horrifically dangerous. It would capsize any boat that ventures onto the lake, and would try to swallow as many of you as it could before retreating to the bottom of the lake to slowly digest you."

  • He will tell of his observances of the creatures in the area, and will offer coin from his hoard in exchange for information on any other creature.

    • "It it is obviously unnatural, and you wish to dispatch it, please feel free to do so, but I will pay coin for detailed observances."

    • "If it is some sort of beast or other natural creature, I would offer you coin from my hoard if you are able to retreat while leaving it alive. I understand if you must kill it, but I will be disappointed."

  • Finally, he will a choice item from his hoard if they kill the gogiteth that is eluding him: a mace with a "greater striking rune."

After the Deals.name: After the Deals
After the Deals.text:
Once they have completed the work he has for them, the dragon will take over the urdefen cavern and move his hoard there. He happily adds all unclaimed items from the cavern to his hoard. He will use rubble to block off all passages except the main one.

He will not molest or approach the heroes again until after they have defeated Belcorra and Gauntlight has collapsed. He will be waiting for them outside the cavern when they emerge from the area leading to the Ebon Doors.

There was a rumble within the immense column that leads upward. Cracks have appeared in its walls, and I sense it has lost all of its magic. You were down there; tell me what happened.

If they tell him of Belcorra's death, he will nod in approval.

It is good that she is gone. This was a mighty deed. Do you intend to claim this cavern, now that you have vanquished her?

The dragon is bracing himself for a battle, and he is not sure he will survive. It should be clear to the heroes that the dragon will fight for the cavern, if necessary.

If they answer in the negative, he will say,

Then I shall claim it instead. You may come and go as you wish, but do not enter my personal cavern without an invitation. I may ocassionally have more work for you, if it interests ones such as yourself.

If they answer in the affirmative, he will say.

I will not surrender this cavern without a fight. Prepare for battle.

Begin combat. The dragon is hoping to be able to catch them in a weakened state. If they wish to retreat back into the area before the Ebon Doors, he will chase them as far as he can and fill the area with his poison breath.

However, it should not be too difficult for them to retreat and deal with him when they are at their full strength.

Later Visits

The next time they venture down into the cavern, there will be a giant hole near the ceiling of the gauntlight tower, and even more cracks have appeared in the walls below.

The dragon now has a shaft that he can use to fly up to the outside word.

The Dragon's New Home.name: The Dragon's New Home
The Dragon's New Home.text:
Once the heroes have vanquished all the urdefen, the dragon will take over its lair. He will inform the heroes when he has done so, and will also warn them not to try to enter the area.

If they wish to parley, he has rigged some hanging chimes outside the main entrance of the cavern. The other entrances he has blocked with rocks and rubble.

The Horned Dragon.name: The Horned Dragon
The Horned Dragon.text:
The horned dragon wandered in not too long ago, from the deeper darklands, looking for new terriroty. It killed the black dragon in single combat and took over his hoard. It then set about exploring the area.

  • It was regularly destroying the Ceustodaemons at I27 Ladder Base until Khurfel himself came to negotiate with him about leaving them alone. In return for his allowing the daemons to stay, Khurfel did not see the harm in answering the dragon's questions about what the lens was on his back, and why he carried it. The dragon then extracted a tribute in exchange for the free movement of the urdefhans in the area.

  • The dragon tangled with the demon in I31 The Barrens several times, but the demon always teleports down the passage when it is injured. It picks a point in the passage past a narrow, twisting passage, thus placing itself out of the dragon's reach. It remains there until it has healed.

    • The dragon has also observed that the urdefhans can pass by the daemon freely.

  • The dragon has observed the deadly Deepwater Dhuthorexes in I39 Deadly Lake, and engaged them in combat several times. They always dive deeply when injured, and the dragon has not opted to follow them. He knows they are unnatural creatures due to their profusion of eyes. He would like to study them more, but he is concerned that they are devouring everything in the lake.

  • It observed the Cauthooj in K41 Island Nest, and is inclined to leave it alone. The bird is about to hatch two eggs, and he would like an opportunity to observe its young.

  • While observing the cauthooj, he noticed the ochre fulcum lens glinting in the shallows. He scared the Cauthooj away long enough to retrieve it. It is now in his hoard.

  • He observed the Ofalth in the Corrupted Garden and attacked it in disgust. The battle was more difficult than he expected because they were both immune to each other's poison. He had to spend a few days recovering from the Wreched Weeps after the battle. He is now trying to coax the garden back to life.

  • He has tried to explore the area beyond the bridge, but he is too large to fit in the passage. So all he knows about this area is it is humanoid cultivated.

  • It engaged the Gogiteth in I49 Gogiteth Cave, but the creature retreated into its cave once it was badly injured, and the dragon was too large to follow. It now flees when it sees him. Most vexing.

He enjoys conversing about any of these subjects, once the heroes prove trustworthy.

Interaction with Belcorra

Belcorra has approached the dragon, and made her pitch regarding her attack on Absalom. He listened to her offer without much interest. One day, he would like to go to the surface world, but as of now, he prefers to continue his work of taming his newly-claimed area. So he told her he would consider her offer, and to come back at a later time. She was annoyed, but had little recourse.

Observations of the Heroes

The dragon will be aware of any battles that the heroes will have with the urdefhen and the daemons, but will endeavor to keep out of sight. Perhaps he watches from the lofty perch high above the hunting lodge, which is visible in the @UUID[JournalEntry.qqYLNFsHGQIZSWkg.JournalEntryPage.uizNE6kRRVENj06X]{Hunting Lodge vignette}.

The heroes interest him, especially if they manage to kill the urdefhen and take the emerald fulcrum lens.

Happily Ever Afters.name: Happily Ever Afters
Happily Ever Afters.text:
Carman and Cynemi?

Assuming the characters have managed to release @UUID[Actor.W5HjwjHOiEYYgLKz]{Natanya Rajani} and the Rajani family from the bloodline curse, a future between Carman is Cynemi is now possible.

However, there are plenty of other options for both Carman and Cynemi. One of your heroes may be interested in either. Carman could try to romance Wrin, Oloria or Yinyasmera. Cynemi could find a future with one of Oloria's drovers, or a town gaurd. Or your players may leave the area and the entire point may become moot.

I'm not even sure what I am going to do with them, so I think I will let the game decide.

Raydolph and Worliwynn?

Raydolph and Worliwynn could up together. Perhaps they will one day get married and build a rustic cabin near Stone Ring Pond.

Klorte and ?

Wryn is a compelling character and is probably a good target for romance with one of your own heroes. The same goes for Yinyasmira and Cynemi.

Either could face some unexpected competition in Klorte.

Korte is looking to settle down now, and has his eye on the town's most eligible females. He believes he would make a powerful and worthy mate. If your heroes decide they are interested in either Wryn or Yinyasmira, it could be a wake-up call to Korte that he needs to make his move.

Dungeon Clean-Up.name: Dungeon Clean-Up
Dungeon Clean-Up.text:
The Mayor will want to debrief the heroes as soon as possible after the collapse of Gauntlight. He will pay his promised reward, plus a bonus, but will question the characters closely.

His questions could uncover some unfinished business. He could offer future rewards to eliminate the following dangers:

Haunts

Some of the more difficult-to-dispel haunts may still be plaguing certain areas such as those in the library. Once dispelled, they no longer have the power to return.

@UUID[JournalEntry.KeWKr2yd8dbppeS5.JournalEntryPage.VZPc5GsIN5eRKSVE]{C05. Spying Hall}

@UUID[JournalEntry.KeWKr2yd8dbppeS5.JournalEntryPage.VoqYMxZSwLDn0l4y]{C32. Furnace room}

Rejuvinating Undead

If at least a month or so has passed since the following undead were defeated, they may have rejuvinated. Once they are killed again, they will be gone for good since Gauntlight is no longer bringing them back. These could include:

@UUID[JournalEntry.uMZ0RiCcPSqsx1Nm.JournalEntryPage.kdk3tW3OgViz0cw5]{B15. Crypt} - Majordomo

@UUID[JournalEntry.uMZ0RiCcPSqsx1Nm.JournalEntryPage.7Cs3QciAV15HwrG8]{B31. Reception Room} - Skeletal Giant

@UUID[JournalEntry.KeWKr2yd8dbppeS5.JournalEntryPage.wAoRY1yKOiu1ocVU]{C34. Temple of the Canker} - Nhakazarin

@UUID[JournalEntry.JT0zCcIwsSpKnbB5.JournalEntryPage.xVfdltaZZguZ35F1]{E25. Gladiators’ Mead Hall} - Bone Gladiator

@UUID[JournalEntry.FwWmtOBFHhvM2gtf.JournalEntryPage.hD6CSfmfkrSopsaw]{H21. Ancients’ Caves} - Empty Death Bodaks

@UUID[JournalEntry.FwWmtOBFHhvM2gtf.JournalEntryPage.Vwd8vMBerJCAoN4N]{H23. Shadowed Dock} - Dread Wraith

Bypassed Monsters

It is possible to get through many of the dungeon levels without destroying every monster, especially starting with level 7:

  • The monsters in @UUID[JournalEntry.OyNcqrpRClyhr8BJ.JournalEntryPage.9ggvXDV6BvojMVBZ]{G17. Stasis Chambers} have likely burst out of their containment cells, fought each other, and scattered throughout level 7 and above. The Witchfire Warden would have departed.

  • Any undefeated abberations in the Farm are still prowling around, especially those in @UUID[JournalEntry.FwWmtOBFHhvM2gtf.JournalEntryPage.EzERYV4NkVvzZeSR]{H15. Fetid Lake}, @UUID[JournalEntry.FwWmtOBFHhvM2gtf.JournalEntryPage.pnTCbvQqpz0arkpz]{H38. Strange Sentry} and @UUID[JournalEntry.FwWmtOBFHhvM2gtf.JournalEntryPage.MFktSOxcOfKGkbb2]{H39. Lair of the Dreamer}.

  • There are many creatures in the hunting grounds that could still be threats. I used the jobs detailed in @UUID[JournalEntry.xjnPxrNNcRBWVegm]{Lv. 9 Side Quest - A Deal-Making Dragon} in order to encourage my heroes to be thorough, but even this may leave behind the creatures that the dragon wanted to spare. This may create a conflict between what the Mayor wants and what the dragon wants.

Graveknight's Armor

If any of your heroes were foolish enough to wear the graveknight's armor, from @UUID[JournalEntry.1vlzl3NJsftNB9Dc.JournalEntryPage.iV9RReXcTyfDbDRq]{I56. Caliddo’s Vigil}, then they will arise as a graveknight (not Caliddo, specifically) and the rest of your heroes will need to defeat him again when the graveknight rises again. Either way, they should have to deal with the armor's curse.

There are several ways to destroy the armor, as described in @UUID[Actor.oXnpdJVN6NIE58W3]{Caliddo Haruvex}'s Rejuvination power.

If the players do not have access to any of those methods, then the lava in @UUID[JournalEntry.OyNcqrpRClyhr8BJ.JournalEntryPage.fK6B6GmATzvRIuh4]{G07. Summoning Chamber} is probably still in place, and is capable of containing the graveknight.

The lava will not destroy the armor, but it will continually destroy the body forming within as it tries to reform over the next 1d10 days, thus sending it into a indefinite creation-destruction loop.

For a more enduring temporary solution, if the heroes next collapse the ceiling and flood the room per the method in the AV journal page linked above, then I don't think the body will be able to reform at all.

It should be up to your players to think of either of these possibilities. Or they may think of other ideas, such as storing it in a vat of acid. Imaginative solutions should work—at least for a while.

A Note on the Wisps

If you use the ideas I presented in @UUID[JournalEntry.zRsCI6WErFnSNEqN.JournalEntryPage.U8sC2KOCcj1ZUgrI]{Belcorra Battle - Preparation} and @UUID[JournalEntry.zRsCI6WErFnSNEqN.JournalEntryPage.jF5LWsgIK5fcAbhJ]{The Final Conflict}, then all the altars in the entire dungeon complex have been desanctified, and all remaining wisps destroyed.

If you used the original story, then the altars that have not been desanctified still remain active enough to produce wisps, as indicated in their respective AV journal entries.

Pathfinder Society Invitation.name: Pathfinder Society Invitation
Pathfinder Society Invitation.text:
By this point, the Pathfinder Society could have heard of the heroes and would probably like to extend the opportunity to make the members of the new Roseguard into full-fledged Agents.

This could be fodder for future adventures.

Future Yldaris?.name: Future Yldaris?
Future Yldaris?.text:
Now that they are free of their oath to Belcorra, the cavern elves of Yldaris would like to return to their homeland.

However, Yldaris has been an important waypoint in the Darklands trade routes, so they would like to turn it over to another group, rather than desert it.

One possiblity is the umbral gnomes, via Calinth Narogblom, the gnomish druid rescued from the urdefhen. He makes at least one visit to Otari to repay his debt to the group, so he is sure to be back.

If that doesn't work out, the heroes could attempt to delve deeper into the darklands to find another group, or they could head to Absalom, where they might find a group through the Darkland entrance via the Undercity.

In any case, it is not entirely up to them, and if the heroes decide to do nothing, then within two years, the umbral gnomes would have taken up residence there.

A Home for Tangletop.name: A Home for Tangletop
A Home for Tangletop.text:
In my game, Tangletop followed the heroes home and then hopped from household to household, searching for the perfect home. He would rather feel like the residents need him.

He considers these places:

  • Odd Stories - The owners are too magically sensitive, and Tangletop would rather a house where he can remain mostly hidden from the residents.

  • Wrin's Wonders - Also too magically sensitive, plus he would rather live indoors.

  • Menhemes Manor - Has lots of children, and Dorienne is a rather sad young lady who might need him.

  • Inkleholtz Manor - Has lots of children, and Alymora looks like she could use his help.

  • Crook's Nook, Crow's Casks or Otari Fishery - taverns are always fun; even if he decides not to live at any of these places, he would probably be a frequent visitor.

DudNoo.name: DudNoo
DudNoo.text:
Assuming he did not become a player character, DudNoo would have established himself in the Otari Garrison and quickly shown himself capable.

At some point, he would go back to Absalom to get some family and friends, and establish a small goblin community in houses under the shadow of the cliff on Manticore Street, near the Garrison.

List of Changes.name: List of Changes
List of Changes.text:
This page contains a detailed guide to changes and additions that is included in this module, arranged by the chapters in which they appear in Abomination Vaults, as well as by other categories that seemed pertinent.

All map pins are colored Gauntlight Blue so they are easy to spot.

Otari

  • Zoomed version of the original Otari map, for easier placement and movement of the player actors around the map. Soundscaped with town, ocean, swamp, and Gauntlight sounds.

  • Added wind chime sounds to Wrin's Wonders.

  • Improved placement of Otari's nighttime building lights.

  • Gauntlight Extras Landing scene, with lights for ambiance, useful for Theater of Mind play.

  • Map of Dawnflower Library

    • Detailed map of Dawnflower Library, including the three shrines and museum area, as well as the cliff walk to the graveyard, with map pins for the encounters, locations, vignettes, music prompts, and prompts to execute macros.

    • Expansion of Deadtide for Otari encounter.

    • Subplot for the theft of the Cooperative Blade.

    • (The merchant actor for Dawnflower Library is included in Tianze's Otari Extras.)

  • Map of the Rowdy Rockfish

    • Noncombat encounter for a Town Meeting after Lasda's rescue.

    • New actors:

      • Ustin Menhemes, Oseph's brother, who runs the family business.

      • Emnala Menhemes, Oseph's wife, who is mentioned in Oseph's journal page in AV.

      • Saamsuma, Cleric of Pharasma.

      • Natanya Rajani, Carman's mother

      • Stewt, a town guard

    • Actors for every named character in Otari, to facilitate the Town Meeting.

    • (The merchant actor for the Rowdy Rockfish is a part of Tianze's Otari Extras.)

  • The NooDupAgNee gang, a gang of goblin adventurers, who have a different goal for entering Abomination Vaults.

    • Includes four gang members, including one with a PC version that a player could pick up after Deadtide for Otari.

    • Subplots and encounters within the Gauntlight dungeons for each remaining member.

  • A new version of the Otari map scene, zoomed in with soundscaping and vignette map pins.

All Gauntlight Levels

  • Added scene regions for improved darkness control.

Level 1

  • New version of Gauntlight Copula, with vignette map pins, lighting, soundscaping and combat music prompts.

  • New version of Level 1 Ruins, with vignette map pins, added sounds and combat music prompts.

  • New token art for Tanglefoot/Spookywisp with journal page.

  • A magical keyring to replace the Rusty Ring of Keys, for player and GM convenience.

  • An inventory item for the broken Mr. Beak doll.

  • A loot actor for the mitflits' fake skeletal guard.

Level 2

  • New version of Level 2 Servant Quarters, with vignette map pins, lighting, soundscaping, and combat music prompts.

  • New version of Otari Graveyard, with vignette map pins, soundscaping and combat music prompts.

  • Dawnflower Library, as mentioned in the Otari section, above.

  • Journals for the Deadtide for Otari and Attack of the Scalathrax encounters in the Otari Graveyard and Dawnflower Library scenes.

  • Added inactive light to the Portal Chamber, to activate as part of the Awaken Portal spell.

  • Added loot actor from journal to the scene for B30 War Room.

  • Prompts for Footsteps of Otari content and macros.

Level 3

  • New version of Level 3 Library, with vignette map pins, lighting, soundscaping and combat music prompts.

  • Encounter with KraDup, member of the NooDupAgNee gang, who is now one of the Canker Cultists.

  • Journal with expanded encounter for the scrivener ghost Chandriu, how to put her to rest, an inventory item for Volluk Azrinae's portrait, and ideas on how this encounter with her can make your players nurse a thorough hatred for Volluk Azrinae.

  • Added a new version for Chandriu's loot actor including missing item and Volluk Azrinae's portrait.

  • Journal for the librarian ghost Jarelle Kalrian, with an alternate way to put her to rest.

  • A magical book satchel, to organize all the books found throughout Gauntlight.

  • A cleric of Pharasma, who should arrive in an interlude between levels 3 and 4, and who has an offer for the heroes.

  • Added inactive light to the Portal Chamber, to activate as part of the Awaken Portal spell.

  • Prompts for Footsteps of Otari content and macros.

Level 4

  • New version of Level 4 Belcorra's Retreat and Smuggler's Refuge, with vignette map pins, lighting, soundscaping and combat music prompts.

  • Ideas on running the werewolf, Jaul Mezmin.

  • A new map, Secluded Clearing, for the area outside the tunnel leading from the Pavilion area. The battle with the werewolf on the 4th level could easily end up here.

  • Subquest, Opening Ghostgate, including new versions of some Roseguard icons.

  • Subquest, Theft of the Cooperative Blade, including a rethinking of Carman's character and background.

  • New history for the Spectral Barrier.

  • Timeline for Volluk Azrinae, after the heroes defeat him for the first time, along with an undead version of a scalathrax for him to raise.

  • Added inactive light to the Portal Chamber, to activate as part of the Awaken Portal spell.

  • Prompts for Footsteps of Otari content and macros.

Level 5

  • New version of Level 5 Arena, with vignette map pins, lighting, soundscaping and combat music prompts.

  • A new arena games side quest, Glory Days, with an arena gamesmaster, ghostly spectators, items, treasure, and arena battle encounters using monsters that already exist in the scene.

  • Additions and revisions to the Arena area and one of the adjacent rooms using specially crafted map tiles that you can activate and deactivate (or hide away in the map margins) as needed. I also have a tiny modification to the entry stairwell.

  • A timeline for Chefkham, in case his timeline runs out before the heroes solve his murder mystery, with his revenge on Jafaki and subsequent activities.

  • Additional inventory items for Chafkham in a new loot actor, to add after he has made all his preparations for his departure.

  • Undead versions of several bosses and monsters from various areas, which Chefkham raises from the dead if he is permitted to run amok.

  • Loot actor for contents of E13 Gladiator Readiness Room - Supply Closet.

  • Added inactive light to the Portal Chamber, to activate as part of the Awaken Portal spell.

Level 6

  • New version of Level 6 Labs, with vignette map pins, lighting, soundscaping and combat music prompts.

  • Added Ethereal walls added around barrels in the Portal Chamber, so the portal light does not shine upon them.

  • Light effects and sounds for the band, Shadow Malice, playing on stage, with all band members in position. This included changes to most of the walls around the tavern so as to flood the nearby hallway with sound, as well as tiles for the light fixtures.

  • Fleshwarping Vats in the care of the Afflicted Irnakurse, including a new NPC to rescue.

  • Fleshwarping Vats in the Main Laboratory.

  • Two members of the NooDupAgNee Gang, with encounters.

  • Minor changes to the Arena via map tiles.

  • Loot actor for the Sarglagon Lair.

  • Added inactive light to the Portal Chamber, to activate as part of the Awaken Portal spell.

  • Added sound-reactive pulse effect to Shadow Malice stage lights for that disco feel.

    • Note: the lights will not activate until you or a player have a highlighted token in the sound's radius.

Level 7

  • New version of Level 7 Prison, with vignette map pins, lighting, soundscaping and combat music prompts.

  • A new level boss, for gamemasters who would rather not roleplay a soul-dealing demon. It includes details on the new boss, her allies, her enemies, her strengths and weaknesses, and her redesign of Urevian’s Domain.

  • Two hags who have a grudge against the Roseguard, and are willing to help the new boos for a shot at revenge on their descendents. They also form a coven with a witchfire on this level, which makes them a true challenge.

  • The second appearance of the Roseguard, who have a role to play in the breaking of the barrier leading to the lift system.

  • A new story for Cynemi, who I made Carman's former paramour, and who is languishing in a prison cell. Includes a new version of her actor with additional inventory items, and a loot actor for the items taken when she was captured.

  • Added the Hellforge Material from the journal to a hidden loot actor in G05 Hellforge.

  • Added loot actor for G17 Stasis Chambers Witchfire Warden.

  • A new fate for Sacuishu in G21 The Secret Void.

  • Added inactive light to the Portal Chamber, to activate as part of the Awaken Portal spell.

  • Added macro to open the Domain Portal.

Level 8

  • New version of Level 8 Farm, with vignette map pins, lighting, soundscaping, lighting and combat music prompts.

  • Journal covering the Dock and Lift area, with the actors that will be in this area, and an alternative way to handle the game mechanics of the lift operations.

  • Journals covering the Belcorra Attacks encounters, with macros and playlists.

  • Journal covering interactions with the caligni, and an alternate way to handle the owb.

  • Journal with a timeline for the continued activities of Sacuishu, from the Prison level.

  • Journal with a timeline for the Elder Child of Belcorra, and his potential comeback after the initial battle.

  • Lighting effect for the Dread Wraith actor.

  • Loot actor for the contents of the Goliath Spider's web, and vehicle actor for one of the boats at the dock.

  • Special lighting for the entrances to the drow areas.

  • Continued appearances by Roseguard members.

  • The return of Shaitan with a friendly new scene for his bazaar. It includes a journal entry and a shop actor.

  • Details of the Rajani Bloodline Curse, with journal entry, an affliction, and the affliction added to Natanya Rajani's character.

  • Added one of the fulcrum lens affect to Urthagul's actor.

Level 9

  • New version of Level 8 Hunting Grounds, Yaldaris and Urdefhan Camp with vignette map pins, soundscapting, lighting and combat music prompts.

  • Added one of the fulcrum lens affect to Khurfel's actor.

  • Hunting Grounds

    • Journals covering a neutral Horned Dragon that replaces the original OGL dragon, with backstory and side quests.

    • Added Reaper Skull Puffballs that were missing from the Hunting Grounds scene.

    • Added boat actor to boathouse.

    • Finished calingi storyline.

  • Yldaris

    • References cavern elves rather than the original OGL dark elves.

    • Added Yldaris Trading Post, with Falxi as the trader, to the stable area.

    • Added music and iridescent lights to the secret tunnel leading to Yldaris, and opposite the secret door in the lizard run.

    • Changed lighting effects in the meditation cave.

    • Added light effects to the trap in The Barrens; also added cavern features to the southern tunnel to support one of the horned dragon's quests.

    • Added lights and sounds to the back of the stable area, so the Shadow Malace band can have one last show before returning to the darklands forever.

    • Added sound-reactive pulse effect to Shadow Malice stage lights for that disco feel.

      • Note: the lights will not activate until you or a player have a highlighted token in the sound's radius.

Level 10

  • New version of Level 10 Temple with vignette map pins, soundscapting, lighting and combat music prompts.

  • Added temple drone sounds in the Challenge rooms.

  • Added sounds throughout the path the heroes must take in the Challenge of Despair, including new wind chime sounds in the J10 Path of Pleasant Memories and J13 Chamber Reflection.

  • Repositioned walls in the pipes leading to the Deadly Swamp.

  • Added tiles to represent the switches that have been turned to the north position.

  • Added swamp sounds.

  • Created scene regions in the Temple with chat macro to remind the GM to check for doom over the rivulets.

  • Added journals for the battle with Belcorra:

    • A journal about preparing for the battle, including a new task for one of the heroes, a summary of how the temple area is currently set up, and an overview of changes I made to the battle.

    • A journal covering the battle itself, and details on a climatic scene afterward, including the Roseguard and an epic confrontation between Nhimbaloth and Pharasma.

Items Without Items

There are many items found throughout Gauntlight that have descriptions in the journals, but do not have actual Foundry items. I have created many of these in order to give the heroes an item to add to their inventory.

(Note: the sections below include items that may also be mentioned above.)

Journals

  • Journals for Gauntlight Maps - a folder of journals for all levels of Gauntlight, detailing changes and additions.

  • Journals for New Maps - a folder of journals for the three original scenes in this module.

  • Gauntlight Vignette Catalog - a folder with journals that have every vignette that shipped with Abomination Vaults, organized into chapters and pinned onto scenes.

  • Character Studies of:

    • Carman Rajani: how I fleshed out his character to make him both a bit of a jerk and more sympathetic, all at the same time. I also completely revised his background, so I could include a generational curse on his family. Plus, there is a love interest for him in the Prison level. I tried to make him both more redeemable and more compelling.

    • Klorte Hengus: he has a long history of challenging anyone who threatens his reputation as the toughest and most powerful warrior in town. He issues a challenge to the heroes.

    • Wrin Sivinxi - how she became claustrophobic, and why she is determined to defeat the threat of Gauntlight.

    • All members of the original Roseguard.

  • Trail of Otari - A timeline of Otari's last days in the dungeons below Gauntlight, along with links to all journal entries that tell Otari's story.

  • Dawnflower Library - room descriptions and two encounters.

  • Doomed Goblin Gang - Story, actors and encounters.

  • Rajani Bloodline Curse - history, affliction, and its effects on Natanya Rajani.

  • Gameplay Reminders - Just a few things that didn't fit elsewhere.

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.JcJjAqOOrVAAGk3l]{After the Adventure}, with ideas on closing some plot threads and continuing adventures.

Items and Sounds

  • New wind chime sound effect for Wrin's shop.

  • Alternatives to some Roseguard Icons, with more useful powers.

  • Belcorra's Key Ring and Librarian's Book Satchel - convenient magic items to organize the many keys and books found throughout the dungeon. Plus a few keys that were created as equipment rather than treasure.

  • Ghost Hunter Dedication codex.

  • Keys, books, portraits and other items that are described or pictured in the journals, but which did not have items.

  • An Afflictions folder, with an assortment of the afflictions encountered throughout Abomination Vaults. I only included conditions that persist after combat for a number of days, and the list is not comprehensive.

    • Now includes Rajani Bloodline Curse.

  • Added all fulcrum lenses to the items menu.

  • New items added by this module.

New Scenes and Maps

  • Dawnflower Library

  • Rowdy Rockfish

  • Secluded Clearing

  • Gauntlight Extras Landing

  • Shaitan's Bazaar

Actors

New Actors, in order of appearance

  • NuuDupAgNee Gang

    • DudNoo

    • KraDup

    • NoxAg

    • PipNee

Belcorra Battle - Setup.name: Belcorra Battle - Setup
Belcorra Battle - Setup.text:
Summary of Changes

I made a few changes to Belcorra's final battle, because, of course I did.

Although the origional ending, where Belcorra decides at the very end that the last thing she wants is an empty death, is quite dramatic, it was not quite in keeping with the lore I had established, where Nhimbaloth denies her followers an empty death so she can use them at some other time.

In order to keep consistant with that lore, I wanted to deny the empty death to Belcorra.

I also thought it would be quite exciting and unforgettable if the heroes were involved in a historic and cataclismic event where two deities actually come together to do battle a second time. For more information about their first encounter, see @UUID[JournalEntry.YbOS6pQRxoWI0Q56.JournalEntryPage.ohFJrgStEzdvGEEU]{Nhimbaloth} and scroll almost to the bottom.

Therefore, one of the heroes is selected to be given the means to actually summon Pharasma when the time is right. She comes for two reasons: to forcibly collect Belcorra's soul, for which she has prepared a special afterlife, and to once again face Nhimbaloth.

Finally, I added some combatants. Since I long planned to have the Roseguard make a limited reappearance, I also added a few creatures on Belcorra's side, to keep things balanced.

If these changes intrigue you, read on!

Preparations before reaching the Temple Level

Early in this module, I first introduced a more active Pharasma when I brought Saam, the priest of Pharasma, into town shortly after the heroes completed the Library level, in order to teach an adventurer the Ghost Hunter dedication.

As they draw near the temple, he will approach one of them for a special task:

  • If one of the heroes follows Pharasma, Saam will choose that hero.

  • If not, if one of the heroes took on the Ghost Hunter Dedication, Saam will choose that person.

  • If not, Saam will choose someone from either the cleric or other divine class, or a champion.

If you have no such character, then, perhaps this ending is not right for your party.

The Psychopomp Mask

Saam presents the chosen hero with what appeared to be an ordinary @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.i5SEEbSALTzH9rgg]{Psychopomp Mask}.

He requests the following:

  • The hero should keep the mask in an easily-accessable spot, without actually investing it or attempting to use it. On a belt would be ideal.

  • During the battle with Belcorra, after the party has invested all three fulcrum lens splinters into Belcorra, if the hero feels Nhimbaloth's presance very strongly (which he will), the hero should smash it.

Saam explains:

I don't know what is to happen when you break it, but I will let you into a Pharasma secret about psychopomp masks. According to their legend, if you are wearing one when you die, the psychopomp that comes to collect your soul will be fooled by the mask and attempt to take it instead, which shatters the mask. This way, you can cheat death, at least for a while.

Do you honestly think that Pharasma's minions are fooled by such a thing? These minor magical items do work, but only because she allows them to work, and to exist.

She wanted them to be somewhat common because every once in a while, Pharasma has another purpose for one of these masks. This is such a time.

He will further add:

It will not break easily if you happen to drop it. Only if you smash it with purpose. Do so if you sense Nhimbaloth's presance.

Preparing the Scene of Battle

Belcorra's Allies

(The ideas here assume that the heroes killed the wisps in J08 Devoruing Chamber instead of allowing them to teleport to the temple room.)

While the battle with Belcorra seemed quite tough, I thought it would be more impactful if it brought more plot threads full circle.

Therefore, I added some tough creatures to this encounter, which are probably still alive:

  • The wisp that stayed behind in I64 Initiates Chamber, beyond the Ebon Doors in the Hunting Grounds. It is to Belcorra's right.

  • Caliddo Haruvex, who by now has rejuvinated from his previous battle with the heroes. He is lurking north of the doors.

The Roseguard

During all this time, the heroes have seen various members of the Roseguard standing guard at level exits. The last real interaction with them was probably on the Farm level.

The Roseguard will take some limited actions in the battle, as detailed in The Final Conflict journal page. They will also help the morrigna take Belcorra away in the final climatic scene.

Pharasma and Nhimbaloth

The tokens for Pharasma and Nhimbaloth are set up at the NE and SW corners of the room, with the following settings:

  • Neither token has a visible image. They only have light effects. In order to surpress the token image, I set their elevations to -1. This way, the light effect works without a token being visible.

    • You may want to test this to ensure the player cannot see the token. A mod may change this behavior. One example of this is the Underground setting in PF2E Toolbelt. Just set it to No Filter.

  • The token visiblity is off to surpress the light effect until you are ready for them. This means that they are not visible at all on the game canvas. I put each of them in front of the notch in the walls in the NE and SW corners. Hover over them to see the token outline.

  • Each token is set up to use the Simple NPC Sheet because their divine stats do not matter.

Scene Regions for Doom Check

As a gamemaster, one of my weaknesses is remembering things like checking for doom when the heroes pass over a rivulet in the heat of combat. This is espeically true for a battle as complicated as this one.

Therefore I created scene regions over all the swamp rivulets, and attached them to a simple chat macro that dumps the relevant journal text into the chat whenever an actor crosses a rivulet during their turn.

@UUID[Macro.LKNokcnnxRzogend]{Player Doom Check}

Apologies if this gets irritating. I also made the regions visible to the GM as an extra reminder.

Overview.text:
Except for the final battle with Belcorra, the majority of changes I made to the temple were to simply to add lights and sounds, with a few small additional changes.

The Final Conflict.name: The Final Conflict
The Final Conflict.text:
Except as noted below, the battle proceeds as described in @UUID[JournalEntry.yn21bNM6kpV4xRol.JournalEntryPage.a9b40LjI7QwLgirk]{J20. Empty Vault}, heading "The Final Battle".

Roseguard Participation

Roseguard will participate as follows:

  • Aesephna will appear the first time someone's health drops below 10%. She will cast her most powerful healing spell on the hero.

  • Vol will appear if the heroes lack the ability to fly and are therefore unable to inflict a touch attack on Belcorra while trying to invest the lenses. She will use her athletics to try to grab Belcorra and wrestle her to the ground. Because they are both ghosts, she is able to do this.

  • Zarmavdian will appear if the presance of Caliddo overbalances the encounter too much. He will attempt to unlease a devastating spell to soak up Caliddo's health.

  • Otari will appear if the heroes are overmatched at any point after this.

I have placed the invisible Roseguard tokens in the swamp pools, where they will probably be out of the way until needed.

Each ghost will appear for the duration of one round. Try not to have more than one active during any one round. After all four ghosts have appeared, use your best judgement when and how to use them again.

Also, if any of the ghosts are damaged, remember that they will be healed by crossing the rivulets, thus using Belcorra's room against her.

Hand-to-Hand Combat with a Ghost

To force the "splinters" from the various Fulcrum Lenses upon Belcorra, it is necessary to make a "melee spell attack roll" upon Belcorra. This is essentially hand-to-hand combat.

If your heroes have not properly prepared for hand-to-hand combat with a flying target, then this battle might be impossible for them to succeed without Vol's help in wrestling Belcorra to the ground.

However, Vol should only be able to help so much. If the heroes cannot engage Belcorra, then the heroes will have to retreat to acquire either a fly spell, or to find some way to bring Belcorra into reach.

Some possible spells and items that I found, that are under 12th level:

  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.A2JfEKe6BZcTG1S8]{Fly} spell

  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.KlJSw919hpN6V9oK]{Potion of Flying (Standard)}

  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.1erd18HS57aCyC6r]{Flying Broomstick}

  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.aaua3vcUXyBFpRe9]{Soaring Wings}

  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.aKoMqPDmVzPI7Q20]{Winged Sandals}

There are probably more.

If your Hero Breaks the Mask

Take your time while playing out this scene. After the heroes have invested the splinters and broken the mask, they have done their part, and they are now observers in a cosmic drama. Use your narrative powers honed over the last 10 dungeon levels to describe the action, while illustrating the action with token movements. However, do not drag it out too much.

Your hero should break the mask when Nhimbaloth makes her appearance just after the final splinter from the fulcrum lenses has been inflicted upon Belcorra.

  • First, introduce Nhimbaloth by activating the invisible token at the southwest end of the chamber.

  • Read the block text in the Nhimbaloth's Entrance heading of @UUID[JournalEntry.yn21bNM6kpV4xRol.JournalEntryPage.a9b40LjI7QwLgirk]{J20. Empty Vault}.

Ideally, your hero should break the mask at this point. The breaking of the mask will summon Pharasma. A @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.z9jEyLrsoBMmh9qg]{Morrigna} will accompany her.

First, activate the invisible token at the northeast end of the chamber, and then read the following:

A whirlwind of ghostly blue energy appears at the northeast end of the chamber, accompanied by the howl of winds that buffet your soul, rather than your flesh.

Next, activate the morrigna next to her. The morrigna is there to collect Belcorra's soul. Pharasma is there to face Nhimbaloth.

A glowing being appears within the torrent of Pharasmid winds. It has a female aspect, and wears long, flowing web-like wrappings and a mask with a web design. It is a morrigna, a psychopomp of Pharsama.

The morrigna will swoop in and attempt to grab Belcorra.

The morrigna swoops toward Belcorra. At the same time, each member of the Roseguard appears above the murky pools. They fly toward Belcorra as she attemps to back away. Together, they surround her as the morrigna lashes Belcorra with her wrappings. The web-like lash wraps around Belcorra with a grip that can trap a ghost. The morrigna pulls her in as she screams one last time.

They all vanish.

At this point, move the Pharasma vortex toward the Nhimbaloth enamation.

A rumble echoes down from the Gauntlight shaft as far above, Gauntlight begins to collapse.

If Your Player Does Not Break the Mask

If your hero forgets to break the mask in the midst of all the action, you might want to consider a reminder. Hopefully, one of the other players will help.

If you decide to let them deal with the consequences, or if the player simply decides not to break the mask, then Belcorra will get her empty death as described in @UUID[JournalEntry.yn21bNM6kpV4xRol.JournalEntryPage.a9b40LjI7QwLgirk]{J20. Empty Vault} under "Destroying Belcorra."

Pharasma will be disappointed in the hero, which might also provide some interesting game fodder. Her @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.boons-and-curses.Item.ParIWsb6B4fdhrHF]{Minor Curse} might be appropriate.

Afterward

Either way, it is no longer safe for the heroes to remain in the room. If necessary, Aesephna will reappear long enough to yell at the heroes to go.

If you wish, you can have the Roseguard appear one final time, once the heroes have reached a semi-safe place, such as the north Challenge room. This interaction should be brief, in which the Roseguard bows to the heroes in thanks, and then disappears forever.

Addiction.name: Addiction
Addiction.description:
Source Gamemastery Guide pg. 120
Track the maximum stage you reach with each drug’s addiction. This maximum stage is separate from your current addiction stage for the drug. The maximum stage can’t be reduced, even if you fully remove the disease. When you take the drug, two things happen: you attempt a saving throw against addiction, and you suppress the effects of addiction for 1 day. Failing a save against addiction caused by taking the drug causes you to go to 1 stage higher than the maximum stage you had previously reached (2 stages higher on a critical failure). If you’re currently suffering from addiction when you attempt a save from taking the drug, you can’t improve your stage; if you succeed at the save, the stage remains the same as it was.

When you attempt your save against addiction each week, the stage you are currently at can’t get worse—it can only stay the same or improve. The conditions from addiction can’t be removed while you are affected by the addiction, and suppressing addiction by taking the drug only avoids the effects—it doesn’t remove the disease.

Saving Throw Fortitude (DC equals that of the drug); 

Onset 1 day; 

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued} (1 week)

Stage 2 fatigued and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (1 week); 

Stage 3 fatigued, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}, and sickened 1 (1 week); 

Stage 4 fatigued, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 2}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} (1 week)

Fungal Rot.description:
• This fast-acting disease causes tiny spores to take root under the skin and blossom in the lungs or in the bloodstream. You become easily winded and incapable of moving quickly. You can’t reduce your sickened condition while afflicted with fungal rot.

Rajani Bloodline Curse.name: Rajani Bloodline Curse
Rajani Bloodline Curse.description:
This curse affects one person at a time. The current cursebearer is Natanya Rajani, Carman's mother.

Stages

Savings Throw: None - when the cursebearer dies, the curse passes automatically to the nearest adult Rajani who is within same generation; otherwise it passes to the nearest adult Rajani in the subsequent generation.

If there are no adults are available, the onset will not begin until the oldest minor is sixteen years old.

The curse will try to exhaust all members of one generation before moving to another, but it can only move to a person who is near the cursebearer at his or her time of death. It can move to a spouse, but only if the marriage produced children.

Onset: 1 Year

Stage 1: Disposition toward family members, romantic attachments and beloved friends changes to Indifferent - 1 year

From this point, the curse has no effect when the accursed is alone. Additionally, the accursed is unable to inflict self-harm.

Stage 2: Disposition toward friends changes to Unfriendly = 1 year, plus the accursed is Stupefied 2 vs. Charisma and Stupefied 1 vs. Wisdom.

Stage 3: Disposition toward acquaintances changes to Unfriendly - 1 year, plus the accursed is Stupefied 4 vs. Charisma and Stupefied 2 vs. Wisdom.

It does not change negative dispositions.

Once the curse reaches Stage 3, it remains at that stage for life unless counteracted with a Cleanse Affliction heightened to Rank 4. Caster DC: 28 (Night Hag).

Sewer Haze.description:

  • Stage 2: Drained 2 and Stupefied 2 (1 day)
  • Stage 3: Drained 3 and Stupefied 3 (1 day)

Belcorra's Journal.name: Belcorra's Journal
Belcorra's Journal.description:
This appears to be a personal journal by Belcorra, herself.

Make these notes visible when appropriate:

The largest book on the northern shelf is a large journal that focuses largely on Belcorra’s hatred of Absalom. It’s written in Aklo, and a hero who spends 8 hours reading it learns of her family history from their exile to poverty and her eventual return to the region to build a lair from which she hoped to exact revenge on the city that disgraced and impoverished her family. The last several pages of the journal document much of her work in building the Abomination Vaults. While the journal doesn’t offer many specific details, it mentions construction of fleshwarping laboratories, arenas where she pitted enemies against monstrous champions for her amusement, prisons, torture chambers, links to the Darklands, and a great temple where “once the Empty Death herself brushed against this fragile world.” Belcorra’s entries often speak of her minions in the abstract, as if bragging about how many have come to serve her in creating the complex, but she only ever mentions one by name: her “amusingly vain” apprentice, Volluk Azrinae. One of the last entries describes how this apprentice arrived from “a community of upstart and meddlesome drow below” to serve Belcorra. The notes don’t provide any further information about this drow community.

Ineffable Hauntings.name: Ineffable Hauntings
Ineffable Hauntings.description: A hero who succeeds at a @Check[type:perception|dc:20]{Perception} while perusing this collection turns up a slender volume called Ineffable Hauntings tucked inside of a larger book about ghosts. This volume contains the formula for the @Compendium[pf2e.spells-srd.c3b6LdLlQDPngNIb]{Create Undead} ritual to create poltergeists. It also contains a detailed, academic analysis of the @Compendium[pf2e.spells-srd.AMEu5zzLN7uCX645]{Ghostly Weapon} spell. A character who can cast 3rd-level arcane or occult spells can use these notes to retrain a 3rd-level spell they know into ghostly weapon with only 1 day of downtime. A wizard can simply transcribe this spell into their spellbook. This book is worth 20 gp.

This missive reads the following:

  1. What The Worm Knows
  2. Grave Feasts
  3. Secrets of the Skull

Transcription will take months, but I’ll try to have these books back to you as soon as possible, my love!

Teleportation Network.description:

The folio details Belcorra's series of linked Teleportation Circles to quickly move around the Abomination Vaults, and it notes the importance of using the Awaken Portal ritual to activate them should time or mischance deplete them of power. The awaken portal ritual is included within the pages.

Found in C35 Secure Collection.

Librarian's Book Satchel.description:
This sturdy crossbody satchel appears to be designed to hold three thick books. In reality, it will hold an entire bookshelf worth of books. The book the wearer is seeking will always be at the ready. If the wearer is not looking for any book in particular, then the last three books that were added to the satchel will be visible.

It only holds books, scrolls and other paper items. There simply will not appear to be room for anything else.

To use the satchel, equip it and drag books into the container area.

Cooperative Blade.name: Cooperative Blade
Cooperative Blade.description:
This +1 striking longsword has a mirror-like blade free of tarnish despite being millennia old.

The Cooperative Blade has the following abilities, which level up with the bearer:

  • 5th Level - Once a day, it can grant an ally who is fighting alongside its bearer the same benefits of the blade's potency and striking runes, as per a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-effects.Item.R5ugeFK3MPwkbv0s]{Effect: Potency Crystal}
  • 8th Level - It gains the Greater Potency Rune effect.
  • 11th Level - It gains the Greater Striking Rune effect, and can share the effects of the additional damage, as described above, as per a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.aSRUX4WGfalK4A5J]{Potency Crystal (Greater)}.

Otari's Thieves' Tools.name: Otari's Thieves' Tools
Otari's Thieves' Tools.description:
You need thieves' tools to Pick Locks or Disable Devices (of some types) using the Thievery skill. Infiltrator thieves' tools add a +1 item bonus to checks to Pick Locks and Disable Devices.

Additionally, Otari's tools has a special enchantment to mitigate failure. Critical failures to Pick a Lock and Disarm a Trap checks become failures, instead.

Thresholds of Truth.name: Thresholds of Truth
Thresholds of Truth.description:
Zarmavdian’s spellbook, Thresholds of Truth, was once a straightforward treatise on arcane and occult lore containing several useful spells. It’s been so heavily
annotated, however, that the original text is hard to read. It’s clear that Zarmavdian wanted to prevent eldritch creatures from manipulating innocent minds, but his spellbook is a treasure trove for those seeking dangerous or inscrutable lore. The
bookseller Morlibint currently keeps this book in his collection at Odd Stories.

Thresholds of Truth provides access to the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.vx5FGEG34AxI2dow.JournalEntryPage.JBPXisA4IdXI9gVn]{Eldritch Researcher} archetype and contains the following spells:

Chafkhem's Magic Circle.name: Chafkhem's Magic Circle
Chafkhem's Magic Circle.description:
This magic circle is specific to Chafkhem only. From his journal entry in Abomination Vaults:

The magic circle at the center of the room assists Chafkhem with maintaining magical energy. The circle gives him a +2 status bonus to skill checks when performing rituals. Additionally, he’s quickened while within the circle but can use the additional action only to Sustain a Spell.

If given the opportunity, Chafkhem will transcribe the magic circle to uphulstery torn off of the divan, and will carry it on his person.

Earthly Tuning Fork.name: Earthly Tuning Fork
Earthly Tuning Fork.description: This crystal and steel tuning fork is used during the casting of a Plane Shift spell that travels the target to the Plane of Earth.

Grandmaster's Missive.name: Grandmaster's Missive
Grandmaster's Missive.description:
Within the scroll is the following missive:

Greetings!

If you find this letter, then you were successful in bringing down the Ghostgate. I also imagine that you have successfully dispatched Volluk Azrinae, along with that horrible voidglutton that holds his leash, since bringing down the Ghostgate would not have been probable if either still lived.

If so, my congratulations.

You may be wondering if this letter is some trick by an agent of Belcorra. Let me assure you that I have never met Belcorra in my life, and even if I had, I would never have agreed to serve her. In fact, her return has disrupted my operations considerably.

In this matter, I am willing to submit to any truth spell you may wish to cast, and there will be no hard feelings. Your suspicion, in this instance, would be appropriate.

But who am I, you may be wondering, and why did I take the trouble to leave you this missive?

Well, on this floor of Gauntlight, there is a wonderous arena. When I first arrived to these Vaults, it was sadly neglected, and had even been used as a nesting site for a particularly monstrous behemoth of a creature. But it has long since been dispatched, the arena tidied up, and the games resumed! I have agreements with the powers that be in this part of the dungeons, and am able to operate the Arena to my heart's content.

Well, that is, I was until recently. In this, I am hoping we can be of mutual assistance to each other. If you care to chat about it, simply head down the Grand Concourse — directly ahead, and through the door opposite this scroll — until you reach the bridge.

At that point, for your own safety, you should stop because the arena has fearsome guards that can kill you with a glance. Simply wait there, and I will be along directly, because I will receive a notification when you open this scroll.

To prove my sincerity, I am enclosing a small item that you may find useful in case you do have an unfortunate encounter with the basilisks. 

I hope you will accept my invitation. I can provide more details when we meet.

 

Sincerely,

The Grandmaster

Scroll of Stone to Flesh (Level 6).name: Scroll of Stone to Flesh (Level 6)
Scroll of Stone to Flesh (Level 6).description:
@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Pr1ruNTbzGn3H9w5]{Stone to Flesh}

Casting a Spell from a scroll requires holding the scroll in one hand and activating it with a Cast a Spell activity using the normal number of actions for that spell.

To Cast a Spell from a scroll, the spell must appear on your spell list. Because you're the one Casting the Spell, use your spell attack roll and spell DC. The spell also gains the appropriate trait for your tradition (arcane, divine, occult, or primal).

Any physical material components and costs are provided when a scroll is created, so you don't need to provide them when Casting a Spell from a scroll. You must replace any required material component for that spell with a somatic component. If the spell requires a focus, you must have that focus to Cast the Spell from a scroll.

Note: To create a scroll or wand of a specific spell, drag the spell from the compendium or compendium browser into the inventory of a PC, NPC, or loot actor.

Spells of Earthen Mystery.description: This is Shaitan's spellbook. It holds at least the spells in his Arcane Prepared Spells, plus an assortment of others.

Aeon Stone (Polished Pebble).name: Aeon Stone (Polished Pebble)
Aeon Stone (Polished Pebble).description:
A polished pebble aeon stone imbues you with the strength of the earth, granting a +1 item bonus to Fortitude saves and DCs against attempts to grapple or swallow you.

The stone's resonant power allows you to cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Wu0xFpewMKRK3HG8]{Grease} as a primal innate spell once per day. You can target only surfaces, not objects, with this spell.

Alchemist Goggles.name: Alchemist Goggles
Alchemist Goggles.description:
These brass goggles are engraved with flame patterns and have thick, heavy lenses.

While worn, they give you a +1 item bonus to Crafting checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.rmwa3OyhTZ2i2AHl]{Craft} alchemical items and a +1 item bonus to attack rolls with alchemical bombs.

You can also ignore lesser cover when making Strikes with alchemical bombs.

Cantrip Deck (Full Pack).name: Cantrip Deck (Full Pack)
Cantrip Deck (Full Pack).description:
In an effort to spread the knowledge of magic as widely as possible, worshippers of Nethys discovered a way to bind cantrips into cards accessible even to non-spellcasters. The deck contains thick parchment cards, each roughly half the size of a playing card. In precise, no-nonsense script, each card simply states the name of its cantrip, color-coded based on its school.

This pack contains 24 cards-one of each cantrip in the Core Rulebook.

Activate 1 or more (envision, Interact)

Effect You envision your desired cantrip, causing its card to rise to the top of the deck, and draw the card. The deck casts that cantrip as a 1st-level spell, with a DC of 15 and a spell attack modifier of +5. The card crumbles into dust as the cantrip takes effect. The activation takes the same number of actions as the cantrip you chose takes to cast.

Caterwaul Sling.description:
Made of shiny brown leather, this +1 striking sling has a single white thread interwoven into its cord.

Activate D Interact (sonic)

Frequency once per day

Effect You pull the white thread free, then whirl the sling in circles at high speed. It lets out an ear-piercing wave of sound. Each creature in a @Template[type:cone|distance:30] takes @Damage[4d6[sonic]] damage (@Check[type:fortitude|dc:21|basic:true|traits:sonic] save). Any creature that fails is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9PR9y0bi4JPKnHPR]{Deafened} for 1 round, or 1 hour on a critical failure.

Ghoul Hide.name: Ghoul Hide
Ghoul Hide.description:
Stitched together from pieces of ghoul skin, this suit of +1 hide armor grants you a +1 item bonus to saving throws against disease and paralysis and makes you immune to the paralysis of ghouls. Ghoul hide with a resilient rune increases the resilient rune's item bonus to saving throws against disease and paralysis by 1 (maximum +4).

Ghoul hide hisses with sibilant hatred at the touch of elves. When worn by a creature with the elf trait, the armor gains the noisy trait.

Horn of Fog.name: Horn of Fog
Horn of Fog.description:
This large ram's horn perpetually glistens with tiny droplets of water, much like condensation.

Activate D Interact

Frequency once per hour

Effect You activate the horn by blowing deeply into it, causing it to issue forth a low blast and cast a 2nd-level @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9XHmC2JgTUIQ1CCm]{Mist} spell. You can Dismiss the mist at any time by blowing a second note on the horn using an Interact action.

Cynemi's Rhythm Bone.name: Cynemi's Rhythm Bone
Cynemi's Rhythm Bone.description:
This small, enchanted bone (most often a jaw) is usually capped with metal at its ends. It's activated by striking it against a hard surface.

Activate 1 Interact

Effect The bone begins recording the next 1 minute of ambient sounds (including speech) that require a DC 15 or lower Perception check to hear. The bone's recording doesn't copy magical auditory effects, such as those of spellcasting, a harpy's song, or a banshee's wail. Once the rhythm bone has been activated in this way, it retains the recorded sound for the rest of its existence and can't be activated this way again.

Activate 1 Interact

Effect The bone replays its recorded sounds.

Craft Requirements Supply a casting of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.atlgGNI1E1Ox3O3a]{Ghost Sound}.

Dialog when played:

(Rustling sound)

Woman: Why do you like me?

Carman: (sleepy) Huh?

Woman: Why are you attracted to me?

Carman: I really like your tail.

Woman: Be serious.

Carman: I do.

Woman: (exasperated sigh)

Carman: Okay, you want an answer? You go first.

Woman: Well ... you're nothing like what I expected.

Carman: Really? Why were you expecting anything at all?

Woman: (flustered) You know ... you have a reputation.

Carman: Really? Tell me all about my . . . reputation.

Woman: Well, I knew you were a bit of a thief and a scoundrel ... from your reputation ... but I didn't expect ... such a impressive physical speciman.

Carman: So I like you for your tail, and you like me for my body. Sounds like we're both pretty shallow.

Woman: It wasn't just your body.

Carman: Well then, what is it? If I'm gonna give you an answer, I want an answer too.

Woman: I think you're just stalling so you can think of something.

Carman: And I think you're doing the same thing.

Woman: You're fun.

Carman: I'm fun? Just in bed?

Woman: No. We're having fun right now, aren't we?

Carman: I guess. I'm just fun? That's it?

Woman: Well, what do you think? That I want your babies?

Carman: I think you do. They'd be physical specimens like me.

Woman: And they might have my tail. Okay, it is your turn now.

Carman: I think you'd rather I did this.

Woman: (exasperated) Carman!

(The rest of the recording is nothing but rustling sounds and an occasional feminine giggle.)

Idriniliss's Notes.name: Idriniliss's Notes
Idriniliss's Notes.description:
These include the information detailed in the @UUID[JournalEntry.OyNcqrpRClyhr8BJ]{G: Prison} journal, including:

  • A first-person journal of how she got here, and who her meetings with Belcorra, plus some miscellaenous notes.

  • Details on her @UUID[JournalEntry.dHfrhlefwZxcjRj1.JournalEntryPage.3phyMR5lLyrs9k10]{Plan of Revenge for Belcorra}.

  • Incomprehensible inspirations granted by her contemplations of the altar

  • Notes on her current alliances within the prison, and her encounters (if any) with Shaitan and Jafaki

  • A scroll written in a cypher that will take time to break (this is regarding the @UUID[JournalEntry.GPXU0ZLTdoTKQPui]{Rajani Bloodline Curse}).

  • Portal note:

There are powerful intruders here, and they are systematically killing everything on this floor. My time here is limited. I have destroyed my only copy of the portal ritual and plan to use it to join the Children and bolster their strength. When I am on the other side, I will cast it again to seal it behind me.

Urevian's Papers.name: Urevian's Papers
Urevian's Papers.description: The contents of Urevian's papers are detailed in @UUID[JournalEntry.OyNcqrpRClyhr8BJ.JournalEntryPage.YSOnwMgSJVzVm31U]{G10. Urevian’s Domain}.

Wooden Shield.name: Wooden Shield
Wooden Shield.description:
Though they come in a variety of shapes and sizes, the protection offered by wooden shields comes from the stoutness of their materials. While wooden shields are less expensive than steel shields, they break more easily.

Hardness HP BT
3 12 6

Ghost Hunter Dedication.name: Ghost Hunter Dedication
Ghost Hunter Dedication.description:
Prerequisites Trained in Occultism or Religion

You have focused your training on hunting and defeating ghosts, spirits, and all manner of haunts. Pick Spirit Lore or Haunt Lore; you become trained in this skill. If you were already trained in both skills, you become trained in a new Lore skill of your choice.

Choose two cantrips from the occult spell list. Each cantrip must have the divination, enchantment, or necromancy trait. You can cast these spells as innate occult spells. You gain access to the Cast a Spell activity if you didn't have it already. You're trained in occult spell attack rolls and spell DCs. You can usually replace material components with somatic components, so you don't need a spell component pouch. Your key spellcasting ability for these spells is Charisma.

Special You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.vx5FGEG34AxI2dow.JournalEntryPage.LL4YD16kPqcGibKG]{Ghost Hunter} archetype.

Ghost Hunter's Codex.name: Ghost Hunter's Codex
Ghost Hunter's Codex.description:
This book is presented by a priest of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QZD0u1jxwz0kj8uI]{Pharasma} to one who finds her favor. 

After a one week period of study, the book will do one of the following, as the Hero decides.

  •  It will teach the Ghost Hunter Dedication, which the hero can add to his or her class feats at the next level up.
  • Or, it will immediately retrain an existing class feat.

After this period of study, the book will crumble into dust.

Once that person has begun to follow the Ghost Hunter Dedication, he or she is free to teach it to others.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.mkp6lhBbTASEmKwY]{Ghost Hunter Dedication}

Awaken Portal.name: Awaken Portal
Awaken Portal.description:
You attempt to reactivate a dormant gate, portal, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.5ZW1w9f4gWlSIuWA]{Teleportation Circle} by infusing it with magical energies. This ritual must be successfully performed twice, once at each location the portal connects. While the teleportation circles and portals found in the Abomination Vaults require no additional cost to awaken, other portals might require rare items or specific materials as a cost for this ritual at the GM's discretion—some portals might even be so powerful that this ritual cannot awaken them at all.

The DC required to successfully awaken a portal varies based on the strength and distance between its end points. For the portals found in the Abomination Vaults Adventure Path, the DC varies according to the dungeon level on which it is located. Use the DCs by Spell Rank section of Table 10-5 to determine the DC for a portal, using the dungeon level in place of spell rank. Thus, activating the portal on the first level of the Abomination Vaults requires a successful DC 15 check, while activating the portal on the fourth level requires a successful DC 23 check.   • Sixth Level @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.abomination-vaults-bestiary.Actor.ceLvlSQsYNORH8oM]{Voidglutton}

  • Ninth Level @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-bestiary-2.Actor.MUVc2ZjwGtlpcuX1]{Gosreg}
  • Tenth Level @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-bestiary.Actor.t4JYGYJqT1CaqKvh]{Shining Child}

Create Undead.name: Create Undead
Create Undead.description:
You transform the target into an undead creature with a level up to that allowed in the Creature Creation Rituals table. There are many versions of this ritual, each specific to a particular type of undead (one ritual for all zombies, one for skeletons, one for ghouls, and so on), and the rituals that create rare undead are also rare. Some forms of undead, such as liches, form using their own unique methods and can't be created with a version of create undead.

Critical Success The target becomes an undead creature of the appropriate type. If it's at least 4 levels lower than you, you can make it a minion. This gives it the minion trait, meaning it can use 2 actions when you command it, and commanding it is a single action that has the auditory and concentrate traits. You can have a maximum of four minions under your control. If it's intelligent and doesn't become a minion, the undead is helpful to you for awakening it, though it's still a horrid and evil creature. If it's unintelligent and doesn't become a minion, you can give it one simple command. It pursues that goal single-mindedly, ignoring any of your subsequent commands.

Success As critical success, except an intelligent undead that doesn't become your minion is only friendly to you, and an unintelligent undead that doesn't become your minion leaves you alone unless you attack it. It marauds the local area rather than following your command.

Failure You fail to create the undead.

Critical Failure You create the undead, but its soul, tortured by your foul necromancy, is full of nothing but hatred for you. It attempts to destroy you.

Creatures Creation Rituals

Crimson Portal Ritual.name: Crimson Portal Ritual
Crimson Portal Ritual.description:
You attempt to call into being a barriar between two walls, pillars, or other substantial structure at least 5' thick.

The ritual consists of the same sequence of chants and gestures repeated three times over the course of the hour.

DC: 24

Critical Success or Success You create the portal. 

Failure You fail to create the portal, and magical backlash leaves you @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 24 hours.

Critical Failure You fail to create the portal, and magical backlash leaves you @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} for 24 hours.

Hunter's Brooch.name: Hunter's Brooch
Hunter's Brooch.description:
While wearing this silver religious symbol of Erastil, you can cast the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.kcelf6IHl3L9VXXg]{Vitality Lash} cantrip as an innate divine spell.

Activate 3 command, Interact

Frequency once per day

Effect By touching a weapon you wield to the symbol and uttering a plea for Erastil's steadying hand, you grant that weapon the deadly d12 trait. Against undead, the weapon instead gains the fatal d12 trait. This blessing lasts for 1 minute, until you score a critical hit with the weapon, or until you aren't wielding the weapon.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-effects.Item.COVEnItnyRmx42EY]{Effect: Hunter's Brooch}

Crimson Fulcrum Lens.name: Crimson Fulcrum Lens
Crimson Fulcrum Lens.description:
This concave lens has a drifting crimson cloud resembling slowly swirling blood within it. While you have the Crimson Fulcrum Lens invested, you seethe with malevolent fury you can barely contain. You gain a +2 item bonus to saving throws against fear effects and a +2 item bonus to your melee Strike damage (this increases to a +4 item bonus to damage if the melee Strike is a jaws attack). You can also activate the lens in the following ways.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-effects.Item.ytqvHyF0oMKbo65P]{Effect: Crimson Fulcrum Lens}

Activate 2 Interact

Frequency once per day

Effect You grasp the Crimson Fulcrum Lens in one hand and make a Strike that doesn't require that hand. The Strike deals an additional 1d8 precision damage (or 2d8 precision damage if you make a jaws Strike) and doesn't count toward your multiple attack penalty.

Activate 2 Interact (attack, possession)

Effect While grasping the lens, make a melee spell attack roll with a modifier of [[/r 1d20+18]]{+18}. On a hit, you force the splinter of Nhimbaloth's essence from the lens to possess the target. You're no longer invested in the lens, and the target gains the benefits as though it had invested the lens but can't activate the lens's other abilities. This effect is permanent, but it can be ended by any effect that removes a possession effect. The lens doesn't have any magical abilities until the possession effect ends; when it does, the essence returns to the lens.

Emerald Fulcrum Lens.name: Emerald Fulcrum Lens
Emerald Fulcrum Lens.description:
